title: Guddi Kesarwani v. State of U.P.
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Surendra Singh-I
disposition: Writ disposed; apply under clause 4.4(a); consider in accordance with law
headnote: The Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a self-contained code with a full-fledged mechanism to redress connection grievances. A person in possession claiming a share in pending partition has a right to seek a new domestic connection under clause 4.4(a). The High Court disposed of the writ without opinion on merits, leaving the petitioner to apply under clause 4.4(a) and directing the licensee to examine and remedy any such application in accordance with law preferably within six weeks.
facts: Guddi Kesarwani sought certiorari against the Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division Rambagh 1A, Prayagraj, and mandamus for a domestic electricity connection. The Electricity Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, Prayagraj, had on 20 July 2022 directed her to apply for a fresh connection. She asserted that the necessary documents had been supplied but not considered, that she was in possession of the house, and that she claimed only a 1/7th share in pending partition suit O.S. No. 11 of 2022.

holding_units.topic: processing of application for new supply
holding_units.holding: Clause 4.4(a) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 governs processing of applications for new supply and requires a complete application with proof of ownership or occupancy (including indemnity as per Annexure 4.2) and, among other documents, owner's consent. The Code is a self-contained enactment with a full-fledged grievance mechanism. The petitioner has a right to seek a new electricity connection under clause 4.4(a). The writ was disposed of without opinion on merits, leaving the petitioner to apply under that clause within a week, with the licensee to examine and remedy any such application strictly in accordance with law preferably within six weeks.

not_decided.point: whether the petitioner was entitled on the existing papers to a domestic connection, including the effect of the pending partition suit and the Executive Engineer's impugned order
not_decided.note: the Court expressly declined to opine on merits and relegated the petitioner to a fresh application under clause 4.4(a)
